items.title: Choose and document the metadata protection model (decision)
items.context: Decide between Approach A (git add -f + check-ignore guard), B (scaffold/validate the ignore-volatile/track-metadata .gitignore allowlist on init/doctor), C (relocate volatile vs persistent), or a combination. Capture as a decision with >=3 preMortem since this is a critical data-loss path. The chosen model must make the bootstrap git-add behavior and the data-loss protection stance mutually consistent.
items.userSees: A decision record states the chosen protection model and rationale; `lattice story_get` reflects the decision and the PLAN gate passes with >=3 preMortem.

items.title: Make worktree bootstrap robust to an ignored story metadata path
items.context: worktree.ts:316 runs `git add .lattice/story/actives/<id>` without -f, which fails with 'paths are ignored' when .lattice is ignored. Implement the chosen model so bootstrap either force-adds with a validated guard or fails with a clear, actionable error/repair instead of an opaque git error.
items.userSees: On a project whose .gitignore would ignore story metadata, worktree bootstrap either succeeds (metadata tracked) or prints a clear remediation message, instead of 'The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files: .lattice'.

items.title: Add a doctor check + scaffolding for the track/ignore invariant
items.context: Add a `lattice doctor` check that flags when story metadata is neither tracked nor protected (the data-loss state), and scaffold/repair the correct ignore-volatile/track-metadata allowlist on init or via a repair command, so new projects are safe by default rather than depending on a hand-crafted .gitignore.
items.userSees: `lattice doctor` reports a clear warning (and offers a repair) when story metadata is untracked-and-unignored, instead of the silent data-loss trap; a freshly-initialized project has metadata protected by default.

items.title: Add regression tests for the data-loss invariant
items.context: Cover: metadata path is tracked (or protected) after bootstrap under both an ignoring and non-ignoring .gitignore; the doctor check detects the unsafe state; bootstrap does not silently leave metadata untracked. Use existing test seams; simulate .gitignore states with fixtures.
items.userSees: `lattice validate` runs the new tests green, proving story metadata cannot end up in the neither-tracked-nor-protected state after bootstrap.
